island: Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Quandamooka Country, Queensland

about.what_this_is: A production graph for the subterranean eco city: the works below the sand, expressed the way a Satisfactory or Dyson Sphere Program player would read it. Resources, processes with real inputs and outputs, buildings, and a four tier tech tree that gates them.
about.whose_design_this_is: This is Luke Nathan Hayes' own long running design, read out of his repos and turned into a machine readable graph. The material stack, the maker loop, the spoil-becomes-supply rule, the two lane method, the C-hour, the locked fund, the aquifer-first rule and the honest labelling all come from his own pages. Nothing about the design was invented for this pack. What was added is arithmetic: stoichiometry, specific energies, rates and footprints, so the graph can be simulated and checked.
about.what_it_is_not: Not a mining proposal. Not a plan to dig. Not a claim that any of this is approved, funded, safe or inevitable. Mining on this island was ended by law and ceased in 2019, and no page of this pack asks for a rerun.

honesty.every_building_is_proposed: Every building in this pack carries existence: proposed. Nothing below the sand may read as a real current island facility, because none of it exists.
honesty.the_frontier_line: Rooms in rock exist. Rooms in unconsolidated, water-saturated island sand do not. Boring through wet sand is solved engineering done under rivers and harbours every week; making habitable rooms down there is the frontier nobody has crossed. This pack holds both truths at once and never blurs them.
honesty.the_water_comes_first: The island's fresh water floats in a lens beneath the sand and that lens is the whole reason people can live here. The first build in this pack is not a machine, it is an open groundwater model. Nothing excavates until the twin exists, the community owns it, and it says the lens is safe.
honesty.scale_is_small_on_purpose: Rates here are island scale and deliberately modest: 3 kg an hour of titanium, 300 g an hour of monazite, 1.2 kg an hour of polysilicon against world plants that make 50,000 tonnes a year. Where a process cannot honestly be rated, it carries no rate rather than an invented one.
honesty.where_the_numbers_come_from: Chemistry is balanced stoichiometry where a reaction exists, and a stated industry mass ratio where it does not. Specific energies are published industrial ranges with the range given. Mass balance is computed by the build script and checked to within 0.5 per cent, not typed by hand.
honesty.what_would_break_this: Three numbers would change most of this pack: the real heavy mineral grade of the remaining sands, the real composition and tonnage of the island waste stream, and the real advance rate of a jacked bore in this ground. None of the three is published. All three are cheap to find out.

country.statement: Minjerribah is Quandamooka Country. This pack claims no cultural authority and implies no endorsement. QYAC is the public doorway for land and sea decisions.
country.native_title: On 4 July 2011 the Federal Court made two consent determinations recognising Quandamooka native title over land and waters on and around North Stradbroke Island. Traditional Natural Resources named in the determination expressly include any clay, soil, sand, ochre, gravel or rock on or below the surface of the determination area. That is the single most important legal fact in this pack: the sand itself is named.
country.national_park: More than half the island is Naree Budjong Djara National Park, declared March 2011, an Indigenous Joint Management Area managed in partnership between QYAC and the state. No works of any kind in this pack may be sited there.
country.consent_rule: Every excavation concept in this pack would require Traditional Owner consent, and must not be sited on or near a place of cultural significance. Consent for a bore does not carry over to room making; it would be sought again. If the answer is no, or not here, or not yet, that is the answer and it is a good one to hear.
cultural_care_specifics: No Quandamooka language word has been used in this pack, and none should be generated into it.
Shell for lime may come only from aquaculture waste or a lawful commercial source. Never from a midden and never from any shell deposit that is or may be culturally significant.
Ochre means something on this island that a pigment plant does not get to borrow. Iron oxide pigment in this pack is ordinary chemistry and is described as colour, not as ochre.
The natural lakes are ruled out for any storage or water scheme first, not last.

register_scale.note: Luke's own five labels, used unchanged so this pack reads the same way his sites do.
register_scale.known: Sourced fact or operating precedent somewhere in the world.
register_scale.modelled: A runnable simulation or calculation, not an operating plant.
register_scale.disputed: A live contest. Reasonable people disagree and this pack does not pick a winner.
register_scale.speculative: Physics permits it; nobody has built it.
register_scale.fictional: Cinematic canon, labelled proudly. Nothing in this data pack carries this label; the Sandworm itself stays on the screen lane where it belongs.

confidence_scale.high: Verified against a published source or settled textbook chemistry.
confidence_scale.medium: Grounded in industry practice with a stated range, or in Luke's own sourced pages.
confidence_scale.low: A modelling placeholder. Treat as a shape, not a number. Replace on contact with real data.

units.rate: kg per minute of nameplate throughput for one building
units.power: kW electrical. Negative power means the process is a net generator.
units.heat: kW thermal. heat_in is drawn from the cascade; heat_out is rejected into it.
units.specific_energy: kWh per kg, with the resource it is measured against named
units.cost: A$ 2026, order of magnitude, not a quote

island_context.estimated_daily_demand_basis: Luke's own energy page, a working estimate for about 2,200 people, labelled as such until checked against real network data.
island_context.rooftop_potential_basis: about 21,000 square metres of viable roof
island_context.footprint_rule: Zero square metres of new land cleared for energy, ever. Roofs, carports, sheds, tanks, structures, shorelines and swell only.
island_context.aquifer_note: About 20 megalitres a day has been pumped from the island aquifer to the mainland since a pipeline was built in 1996, reported as up to 60 per cent of the Redlands supply, though an October 2024 figure puts the mainland and southern Moreton Bay islands share at 40 per cent. Island community use is about 1.6 megalitres a day. Eight Olympic pools a day leave; the community runs on well under one.
island_context.mining_history: Mineral sand mining ran here for around eighty years. The North Stradbroke Island Protection and Sustainability Act 2011 phased it out and the Enterprise mine, the last operating, closed in 2019. Vance mined silica sand for glass; Enterprise and Yarraman mined the heavy minerals. The minerals in this pack are documented because somebody dug them up and sold them, which is the strongest evidence a mineral claim can have and also the reason the island is wary.

power_reality_check.note: This is the honest sting in the tail, and it is why the numbers were computed rather than asserted. Building every process to tier 3 puts about 2478 kW of connected load under the sand. At only 40 per cent utilisation that is roughly 23792 kWh a day against an island that is estimated to use about 30,000, and rooftops that could carry about 19,000. The generation described inside this pack is 54 kW. The gap is not an error in the arithmetic; it is the arithmetic telling the truth. The harvest has to be built first, at a scale nothing here yet describes, and the deepest and hottest processes are the last things you build, not the first.
power_reality_check.the_three_worst_offenders: The pumped hydro pump at 2,000 kW, the carbon furnace hall at 456 kW (silicon 360, carbide 96) and the sand battery charger at 500 kW are about 54 per cent of the connected load between them. Two of the three are the deepest tiers, and the third only ever runs on surplus.
power_reality_check.what_this_means_for_play: A player who rushes the carbon furnace hall should black out the island. That is the intended lesson and it should be enforced, not softened.

thermal_cascade.principle: Heat only ever flows one way, so this is a staircase, not a circle. Each step uses what the step above had finished with, until the last of it is warming a room. Underground there is no sky to throw it at, which turns heat rejection from a cost into the design.

sinks: nothing above them: this is the top of the staircase

thermal_cascade.cold_side: Separating air for welding gases and life support leaves liquid nitrogen. Piped through the food store before the gas goes and does its industrial job, that cold runs long term cold storage as a by-product rather than a cost.

closed_loops.name: The magnesium and chlorine loop
closed_loops.arithmetic: Kroll takes 0.051 kg of magnesium a minute and returns 0.199 kg of magnesium chloride. Electrolysis of 0.392 kg of that salt gives back 0.100 kg of magnesium and 0.292 kg of chlorine. Energy, ore and seawater go in; the magnesium and chlorine keep going round.
closed_loops.honest_gap: This pack has not run a full chlorine mass balance across all four chlorinating processes, so the claim that no top-up chlorine is needed is not made.

closed_loops.name: The silicon tetrachloride loop
closed_loops.closes: only if the acid is routed
closed_loops.arithmetic: Hydrolysing silicon tetrachloride throws off four molecules of hydrochloric acid for every one of the chloride: 0.121 kg a minute here. Silicone hydrolysis adds another 0.197 kg. Methyl chloride synthesis consumes 0.202 kg. Route the acid back and the circle closes; do not, and you have swapped one stream for another.
closed_loops.honest_gap: That routing is the part most versions of this idea leave unsaid, and Luke names it himself. It is stated here as arithmetic rather than assumed.

closed_loops.name: The pigment chlorine loop
closed_loops.arithmetic: Chlorination consumes 0.299 kg of chlorine a minute to make titanium tetrachloride. Oxidising that back to pigment releases 0.266 kg. The 0.033 kg shortfall is what the chlor-alkali cell has to make up, and it is stated rather than glossed.

closed_loops.name: The sulfur loop
closed_loops.arithmetic: Calcining copperas gives 0.036 kg a minute of sulfur dioxide. The acid plant is rated at 0.065 kg a minute of feed, so it runs part loaded and about half the sulfuric acid still needs elemental sulfur brought in.

closed_loops.name: The carbon loop
closed_loops.arithmetic: Biochar reduces sand to silicon and carbide, the furnaces breathe 1.472 kg a minute of carbon monoxide, the afterburner turns that into 2.313 kg of carbon dioxide and about 248 kW of high grade heat, and the carbon dioxide feeds methanol, the algae columns and the refrigeration loop.
closed_loops.honest_gap: Capturing carbon dioxide is easy to say and hard to do. Exactly how to catch it, at what purity and at what parasitic energy cost, is a choice nobody here has made.

closed_loops.name: The thermal cascade
path: every furnace and reactor in the pack
closed_loops.arithmetic: Heat only flows one way. This is a staircase, not a circle, and calling it a loop would be the dishonest move.

orphan_streams.note: Spent acid from monazite cracking, carrying radium and actinium: the things thorium turns into as it falls apart. No stated fate. This is the stream that most needs one and the strongest single argument for leaving the monazite where it is.

The awkward majority. Monazite is mostly light rare earths, so cerium and lanthanum are the bulk of what comes out, and this system has a job for neodymium. Routing the minority and calling it a loop is a fair criticism.
The spent phosphate matrix. Plausibly a fertiliser and nobody has pinned that route down.
From magnesium recovery. Road dust suppression and brine are the usual outlets and neither is assigned here.
Reactive, and a real hazardous waste at scale.
Board resin after metal recovery. No home.
Acidic, phenolic, and a genuine wastewater treatment load that pyrolysis pitches usually skip.
Even after mineral recovery, the brine still has to go somewhere and its discharge is a marine ecology question, not a solved one.
About 7.8 per cent of the tip stream still gets buried in this design. The honest goal for this list is nothing. It is not nothing.
Weak spent acid from the sulfate route. Reconcentration is possible and is not costed here.
From the speculative bio-leach. Still NORM.

imports_that_never_close.note: Flat glass wants soda ash and the sea gives table salt. No honest local route found.
The geopolymer needs a reactive aluminosilicate. Whether a usable kaolin exists on Minjerribah in workable quantity was not verified.
About half the sulfuric acid, because the copperas loop only supplies the other half.

reality_gates.name: Traditional Owner consent
reality_gates.note: Not a permit to be obtained. A relationship, and a right to refuse. Sought again for each stage, not carried over.

reality_gates.name: Sea Country consent
reality_gates.note: Anything in the water or on the shore. Reefs, shoreline work, wave devices, placed sand.

reality_gates.name: Cultural heritage clearance
reality_gates.held_by: Traditional Owners and the state cultural heritage process
reality_gates.note: No excavation is sited on or near a place of cultural significance. Where that cannot be established, the answer is no.

reality_gates.name: Aquifer twin pass
reality_gates.held_by: The community, through an open MODFLOW model of the freshwater lens
reality_gates.note: The lens comes before the tunnel, first and every time. You cannot negotiate what you cannot see.

reality_gates.name: National park exclusion
reality_gates.note: More than half the island. Nothing here goes there.

reality_gates.name: Mining ended by law
reality_gates.held_by: North Stradbroke Island Protection and Sustainability Act 2011
reality_gates.note: Operations ceased 2019. This pack is not a mining proposal and does not want to be one.

reality_gates.name: Radiation management licence
reality_gates.held_by: Queensland radiation safety regulation and ARPANSA guidance
reality_gates.note: The moment monazite is concentrated this is a licensed radiation workplace: monitored workers, contained dust, a plan for the whole decay chain.

reality_gates.name: Nuclear prohibition
reality_gates.held_by: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 section 140A and Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Act 1998 section 10
reality_gates.note: Federal law prohibits nuclear power installations. This pack contains no reactor. The thorium is banked in glass and stewarded, not burned.

reality_gates.name: Coastal management approval
reality_gates.held_by: Queensland coastal management and Redland City Council
reality_gates.note: Shoreline works, erosion control, placed sand.

reality_gates.name: Marine ecology review
reality_gates.held_by: Independent review before anything enters the water
reality_gates.note: No blade a living thing can reach. Noise, sediment, turtles, dugong, dolphins.

reality_gates.name: Engineering certification
reality_gates.note: Occupied underground space, ventilation, egress, fire, structural.

reality_gates.name: Community vote
reality_gates.note: Held with full information and a real option to refuse. A vote you cannot lose is not a vote.

simulation_hooks.tick_note: One sim tick is ten sim-minutes, so a process rate of x kg per minute delivers 10x per tick. Use world.clock, never Date.now.
simulation_hooks.determinism_note: Any variation in yield, breakdown or grade must come from world.rng.stream('subterranean'). Never Math.random.
failure_modes: Power deficit: the island browns out before the furnace reaches temperature. Deepest and hottest processes trip first.
Heat deficit: block cure and desalination stall when the furnaces are down, because they are customers of the cascade and not independent.
Consent withdrawn: excavation stops that tick and does not resume until it is given again. There is no override.
Lens drawdown breach: the aquifer twin flags it and every excavation process halts. This is a hard stop, not a penalty.
Orphan stream overflow: if a stream with no destination accumulates past its store, the tier is not allowed to advance.
simulation_hooks.player_legibility: The three numbers to put on the panel are the connected load against generation, the orphan stream total, and the residual to landfill. If those three are getting worse, the city is not working, however good the throughput looks.

design_provenance.what: The spine. alchemy.html is the transformation tree and the zero waste audit; tunnels.html, boring.html, rooms.html and dig.html are the excavation logic; thermal.html and storage.html are the heat and battery logic; materials.html plus quartz, zircon, titanium and monazite are the mineral stack; reclaim.html is the tip loop; walls.html is the four legal walls; capital.html and care.html are the ledger and the C-hour; corridor.html is the line on the ground.

material-stack.html, in-situ-resources.html, maker-loop.html, subterranean-city.html, ledger.html, energy-resilience.html, trust-work.html, ai-robotics.html. The reality gates, the public ledger rules and the maker loop posture come from here.
The spoil ledger discipline, the spoil-becomes-supply framing, the reef and sand battery destinations, and the rule that a material stream needs a passport, a review path and a reason to exist.

The Silica Citadel concept: fabrication nodes rather than factories, import knowledge and export nothing, the anthropogenic ore body, lateral wall mining and osteomorphic block placement, transcritical carbon dioxide cooling, and the 500 year design life.
The surface end of the corridor and the explicit note that Sandworm-style subterranean systems are long range research, not a promise to dig under Ballow Road.

building-a-civilization-from-sand.md and civilisation-of-sand.md for the materials pipeline, the greenhouse and algae logic, the digital twin as planning tool, and the deliberate off-world extensibility.

resources.name: Dune sand, as it lies
resources.note: Over 90 per cent of the island by weight. Quartz with a small heavy mineral fraction.

resources.name: Saturated sand at the tunnel face
resources.note: About 1,590 kg of solids and 400 kg of pore water per cubic metre below the water table.

resources.name: Washed quartz sand
resources.note: SiO2. Unusually clean here, which is exactly why mining it was worth eighty years.

resources.name: Heavy mineral concentrate
resources.note: The dark seams the waves concentrated. Grade assumed at 1 per cent of excavated sand, unverified.

resources.name: Ilmenite
resources.note: The bulk heavy mineral: titanium and iron in one black grain. Magnetic.

resources.name: Rutile
resources.note: The best natural ore of titanium there is.

resources.name: Zircon
resources.note: Tough, heat proof, and carrying a whisper of natural radioactivity that only matters when you process a lot at once.

resources.name: Monazite
resources.note: Naturally occurring radioactive material. Licensed handling only.

resources.name: Dewatered spoil sand
resources.note: The tunnel does not make spoil. It makes supply.

resources.name: Bentonite slurry
resources.note: Recirculates. Only the makeup is a real consumption.

resources.name: Seawater
resources.note: The input that never runs out.

resources.name: Desalination brine
resources.note: Usually a discharge headache. Here it is the magnesium and salt feedstock.

resources.name: Spent brine after mineral recovery
resources.note: Still has to go somewhere. Discharge remains an open marine ecology question.

resources.name: Freshwater lens groundwater
resources.note: Non-negotiable. This pack draws none of it for industry. The lens already carries about 20 megalitres a day leaving for the mainland.

resources.name: Liquid nitrogen
resources.note: Its cold runs the food store before the gas does its industrial job.

resources.name: Sodium silicate, water glass
resources.note: The zircon plant's effluent is the builder's reagent.

resources.name: Zirconia ceramic part
resources.note: Cutter heads, pump bearings, furnace linings, blades, thermal barriers.

resources.name: Silicon tetrachloride
resources.hazard: fumes to hydrochloric acid on contact with water

resources.name: Metallurgical grade silicon
resources.note: About 99 per cent pure. Good for alloys and silicones, nowhere near good enough for a solar cell.

resources.name: Solar grade polysilicon
resources.note: 99.9999 per cent. The step every glib line skips.

resources.name: Silica fume
resources.note: Straight into the block mix as a pozzolan.

resources.name: Silica aerogel
resources.note: Among the best insulation there is. It is what lets the sand battery hold heat for weeks.

resources.name: Carbon dioxide
resources.note: Refrigerant, aerogel drying fluid, methanol feed, algae food. Never simply vented in this design.

resources.name: Carbon monoxide
resources.hazard: toxic, and a fuel worth 10.1 MJ per kg

resources.name: Biochar
resources.note: The reductant that turns sand into silicon, and also soil improver, filter media and the black in the paint.

resources.name: Syngas
resources.note: About 5.5 MJ per kg for pyrolysis gas.

resources.name: Pyrolysis water
resources.note: A wastewater stream needing treatment. Named rather than quietly dropped.

resources.name: Mycelium insulation panel
resources.note: Chars instead of melting, which matters a great deal in a sealed space.

resources.name: Mixed tip waste
resources.note: The richest ore on this island, and it arrives by truck already refined.

resources.name: Residual to landfill
resources.note: The number this whole pack exists to shrink. It is not zero and saying so is the point.

resources.name: Circuit boards
resources.note: The densest ore in the whole stream.

resources.name: Soda ash, imported
resources.note: The honest catch. Evaporating seawater gives you table salt, not soda ash.

resources.name: Limestone or aquaculture shell
resources.note: Never from a midden. Never from a culturally significant shell deposit.

resources.name: Crushed shell
resources.note: Aquaculture waste or lawful commercial source only.

resources.name: Kaolin clay
resources.note: Local availability on Minjerribah unverified. Treat as an import until proven.

resources.name: Titania slag
resources.note: Assays about 85 per cent titanium dioxide, not pure.

resources.name: Titanium sponge
resources.note: Corrosion proof in seawater for a lifetime. About 34 kWh per kg across the whole chain.

resources.name: Copperas, iron sulfate heptahydrate
resources.note: A genuine disposal headache at pigment plants worldwide. Here it is the red and yellow pigment feed.

resources.name: Iron oxide pigment, red and yellow
Sodium phosphate liquor
resources.note: A plausible fertiliser and nobody has pinned that route down.

resources.name: Cerium and lanthanum oxide
resources.note: The awkward majority. Polishing compound and catalyst are the honest uses, and this pack has not found them a home at island scale.

resources.name: Vitrified thorium log
resources.note: Banked, monitored, not burned.

resources.name: Spent acid carrying radium and actinium
resources.note: The stream that most needs a stated fate and does not have one.

resources.name: Silicon kerf swarf
resources.note: Straight back into the melt. The unglamorous recoveries are what make an audit honest.

resources.name: C-hour
resources.note: A record, not money. Never sold back to the person who did it.

resources.name: Consent
resources.note: Not a resource the player can manufacture. It is given or it is not.

tech_tree.name: The bench and the ledger
tech_tree.summary: Everything on this rung is lawful today, costs almost nothing, and needs nobody's permission but the landholder's. Sand literacy, repair, the tip loop, rooftop power, and the two records that make the rest legible.
unlock_conditions: none, this is where anyone starts
tech_tree.completion_test: A material passport exists for one real object, a C-hour has been recorded for one real hour of work, and the tip has caught one thing that would otherwise have been buried.

tech_tree.name: The first bore and the first melt
tech_tree.summary: A two metre logistics bore, the size civil contractors already dig and insure. The spoil becomes supply: washed sand, separated minerals, glass, cement-free blocks, reef modules and shoreline repair. Heat starts cascading instead of escaping.
unlock_conditions: aquifer twin built, published and community owned
the twin shows no unacceptable drawdown of the freshwater lens for the proposed method
Traditional Owner consent obtained through QYAC for the specific site
cultural heritage clearance for the specific site
site is outside Naree Budjong Djara National Park and outside any place of cultural significance
engineering and geotechnical certification for a jacked bore below the water table
tech_tree.completion_test: One hundred metres bored, every cubic metre of spoil accounted for by destination, and the lens monitoring showing no change beyond the agreed band.

tech_tree.name: The refinery under the dune
tech_tree.register: known for the individual processes, modelled for the integration
tech_tree.summary: The chemistry rung. Chlor-alkali, magnesium from brine, titanium, both pigment routes and the loop between them, zircon split two ways, silicon, silicone, aerogel, the living corridor and the metal recovery hall. Most of these are real industrial chemistry running somewhere in the world today. The island scale integration is the part that is only modelled.
unlock_conditions: tier 2 complete and running for at least one full wet season
radiation management licence in place before any monazite is concentrated
a signed island energy plan showing the harvest is built before the load
hazardous materials, emergency egress and ventilation certification for occupied underground space
a published mass balance for chlorine across every chlorinating process
tech_tree.completion_test: The zero waste audit shows every named stream with a destination, and the orphan list is shorter than it was when the tier opened.

tech_tree.name: Deep time, gated
tech_tree.summary: The frontier and the things behind walls. Lateral wall mining, in-situ glass lining, polysilicon and cells, the monazite and thorium branch, underground pumped hydro. This rung is where the honest answer is usually no, or not yet, and the work moves to simulation and cinema rather than to the bin.
unlock_conditions: a community vote, held with full information and a real option to refuse
Traditional Owner consent renewed specifically for room making, not carried over from the bore
the aquifer twin validated against at least three years of measured lens data, not just calibrated
for the monazite branch: a radiation licence, a decay chain plan, and a stated fate for the spent acid
for anything nuclear: a change in federal law that does not exist today
tech_tree.completion_test: There is no completion test. This tier is designed so a player can reach it, look at it, and reasonably decide not to build it.

buildings.name: Maker bench
buildings.siting: Surface, an existing shed. The Ballow Road hub and the maker-space proposal are the named candidates in Luke's own repos.

buildings.name: Tip loop shed
buildings.siting: Beside the existing waste and recycling facility. Surface, no excavation.

buildings.name: Pyrolysis shed
buildings.siting: Surface, industrial setback, air quality assessed.

buildings.name: Rooftop and structure solar array
buildings.siting: Existing roofs, carports, sheds, tanks and fences only. Zero new land cleared.

buildings.name: Open data lab
buildings.siting: Any room with power. The ferry terminal open data lab and the Ballow Road evidence map are the two real ones already public.

buildings.name: Microtunnel drive shaft and jacking pit
buildings.siting: Surface pit, cleared and previously disturbed ground only. Never on or near a place of cultural significance. Outside the national park.

buildings.name: Mineral separation line
buildings.siting: Enclosed. Dust containment is not optional once monazite is in the feed.

buildings.name: Sand thermal battery silo
buildings.siting: Below ground on purpose: the surrounding sand is free insulation and there is no sky to lose heat to.

buildings.name: Oscillating water column breakwater
buildings.siting: Inside a coastal structure that would exist anyway. Never a new structure built only for power.

buildings.name: Chlorination plant
buildings.siting: Sealed, scrubbed, with its own containment. Chlorine chemistry is the highest hazard block in this pack after the NORM plant.

buildings.name: Carbon furnace hall
buildings.siting: Deep, because it is the hottest room in the city and its reject heat has the furthest to fall down the cascade.

buildings.name: Living corridor
buildings.siting: The corridor wall itself. Algae columns and mushroom rooms are the air handling, not a garden feature.

buildings.name: Lateral wall mining head
buildings.siting: Nowhere without consent. Not on or near a place of cultural significance, not in the national park, not until the aquifer twin says the lens is untouched.

buildings.name: Radioactive materials plant
buildings.siting: Licensed facility, contained ventilation, monitored workers, whole decay chain plan, and a community that voted for it in daylight. If any of those is missing it is not built.

buildings.name: Pumped hydro void and pond
buildings.siting: Sealed void below, pond above on a rehabilitated mine bench. Never the natural lakes, which are ruled out first, not last.

buildings.name: Device fabrication, unreachable
buildings.siting: Not sited, not costed, not near. Present in the tree so the player can see the edge of what an island can do alone.

processes.name: Hand lens sorting bench
processes.notes: The cheapest first step into material literacy: tell quartz from the heavy fraction by colour, grain and weight. Sample scale only.

processes.name: Magnet bench separation
processes.notes: Ilmenite is magnetic. Drag a magnet through black sand and the iron-titanium fraction lifts out. No lab required.

processes.name: Tip triage bay
processes.notes: Gate one of the tip loop: one sorting bay, a roof and someone whose job it is to look. The split shown here is a modelling assumption. Nobody has published a composition audit for this island's waste stream, and that audit is the single cheapest thing anyone could do to make this whole pack real.

processes.name: Repair bench
processes.notes: Repair cafes and Men's Sheds already prove the model across the country. Nothing here is new; it is an assembly job.

processes.name: Cullet crusher

specific_energy.basis: small jaw and roll crusher on glass, industry rule of thumb

processes.notes: It came from sand and it goes back to sand. Cullet cuts glass furnace energy sharply, which is why the furnace downstream runs at half virgin batch.

specific_energy.basis: horizontal grinder on mixed green waste

processes.name: Compost windrow
processes.notes: Mass loss to carbon dioxide and water vapour is the composting reaction itself, not a rounding error. Roughly 47 per cent of the wet feed leaves as gas and vapour.

processes.name: Biochar retort (slow pyrolysis, about 500 C)
processes.chemistry: Thermal decomposition of lignocellulose without oxygen. Yields are a mass split, not a stoichiometric equation.
processes.byproduct_routing: biochar to carbothermic-silicon, acheson-sic and ilmenite-smelt as the reductant; syngas to syngas-chp; bio-oil to fuel; pyrolysis water is a wastewater stream needing treatment.
processes.notes: The quiet hub the whole tree hangs off: one furnace, three useful streams. Yields of 26 per cent char, 25 per cent oil, 22 per cent gas and 27 per cent water are mid-range for slow pyrolysis of woody feed with about 15 per cent moisture. It will not make battery-grade graphite; biomass char is the wrong carbon for that.

processes.name: Rooftop and structure solar harvest

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: The footprint rule: roofs, carports, sheds, tanks and structures only. Zero square metres of new land cleared, ever. 480 m2 of existing roof carries about 100 kW peak at current module efficiency, and south east Queensland yield is about 4.3 kWh per kW peak per day.

processes.name: Bench sand heat cell

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Silica sand holds about 0.8 kJ per kilogram per kelvin. 28 kg lifted 280 K stores about 6.3 MJ, or 1.7 kWh, before losses. The same physics as the Finnish silo, at a size you can put on a table.

processes.name: Aquifer twin run (MODFLOW)

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: The flagship of the whole pack is not a machine, it is a model. An open groundwater twin of the freshwater lens, built in MODFLOW from the island's published hydrology. Nothing below the sand unlocks until this exists and the community owns it. Students can start this today.

processes.name: Material passport issue

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Every sample or object carries source, recipe, safety limit, repair path, steward and end-of-life note. Without this the whole graph is just a story about sand.

processes.name: C-hour record

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: One C-hour is a record that one real hour of community work happened: a real person, a real hour, signed off. It is deliberately not money. It has no price, it is not traded, and it is never sold back to the person who did it. Not legislated anywhere, and the island has not built it yet.

processes.name: Slurry shield microtunnel bore, 2 m
processes.chemistry: Ground displacement, not chemistry. Pressurised bentonite slurry balances the aquifer at the face so the saturated sand cannot slump in.
processes.byproduct_routing: spoil slurry to slurry-separation; recovered bentonite recirculates.
processes.notes: A 2 m bore is about a doorway laid on its side, the size civil contractors already dig and insure every day, jacked unmanned for sewers and cables. In-situ saturated dune sand taken at 1,990 kg per cubic metre, being about 1,590 kg of solids and 400 kg of pore water. Modelled at about 46 kWh per cubic metre of excavated ground. Advance rate is the least certain number here: quoted rates vary tenfold between estimates, so 15 m a day is a target, not a promise.

processes.name: Slurry separation plant
processes.notes: Cyclones, screens and a centrifuge. Standard kit on every slurry tunnel drive in the world. Recovered bentonite returns to the face, which is what makes the fluid a circuit rather than a consumable.

processes.name: Spiral classifier and wash
processes.notes: Heavy mineral content is modelled at 1.0 per cent of the excavated sand. This is the weakest number in the pack. Luke's own materials page says plainly that the actual tonnages and remaining grades are not known well enough to print, and no public assay for the remaining island sands was found for this pack.

processes.name: Heavy mineral separation line
processes.notes: Wet gravity, then dry magnetic and electrostatic separation, which is why the dryer heat sits here. The assemblage split (55 per cent ilmenite, 20 per cent zircon, 10 per cent rutile, 1 per cent monazite, 14 per cent other) is a modelling assumption from the general eastern Australian mineral sands pattern, not an island assay. The moment monazite is concentrated, this becomes a licensed radiation workplace with monitored workers and contained dust.

processes.name: All-electric glass melter
processes.chemistry: Na2CO3 -> Na2O + CO2 and CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 within a soda lime silica batch. The carbon dioxide comes off the carbonates, not the sand.

specific_energy.basis: all-electric melter at 50 per cent cullet; industry range 0.9 to 1.4 kWh per kg

processes.byproduct_routing: batch carbon dioxide to co2-heat-pump, methanol-synth and algae-photobioreactor. Off-spec glass crushed back to cullet.
processes.notes: The honest catch, and Luke names it himself: flat glass wants soda ash, and evaporating seawater gives you table salt, not soda ash. Soda ash stays an import in this pack until someone finds an honest local route. Chemistry checks out: 0.60 kg soda ash gives 0.249 kg carbon dioxide and 0.55 kg carbonate gives 0.242 kg, which is the 0.49 kg shown.

processes.name: Clay calciner (metakaolin)
processes.chemistry: Al2Si2O5(OH)4 -> Al2Si2O7 + 2 H2O at about 750 C.

specific_energy.basis: flash calcination of kaolin, 700 to 800 C, thermal

processes.notes: This is the honest gap in the geopolymer story. Quartz is inert filler, so a geopolymer needs a reactive aluminosilicate as well as an alkali activator. Whether a usable kaolin clay exists on Minjerribah in workable quantity was not verified for this pack. Until it is, treat calcined clay as an import and the block cost rises accordingly. Heat is supplied from syngas or the cascade, not from electricity.

processes.name: Geopolymer block press

specific_energy.basis: mixing and hydraulic pressing, electrical only

processes.byproduct_routing: sodium silicate activator comes from zircon-caustic-fusion; trim offcut is crushed back into the mix.
processes.notes: Cement free, so there is no clinker calcination carbon dioxide. Curing at 60 C comes off the waste heat cascade, which is the point: the block plant is a customer for heat the furnaces would otherwise throw away. Interlocking, mortar-free block geometry that can shift and settle is a drawn design idea, not something built at this size.

processes.name: Paver and tile press
processes.notes: The backyard-scale end. A household could press its own tiles and pavers and mend them when they crack. For the island's own homes, not for export.

processes.name: Reef module casting (oyster-crete)
processes.notes: Rough texture and hole pattern designed habitat-first. Shellfish reefs are proven in bays around the world; putting one here is only an idea and it waits on the people who hold this water. Crushed shell must come from aquaculture waste or a lawful commercial source. Never from a midden, and never from a shell deposit of cultural significance.

processes.name: Dune and shoreline sand placement
processes.notes: The cheap destination, and where most spoil would honestly go: dune foot repair, blowout patching, access-track sand ladders, living shoreline edges. Little more than the energy to carry and shape it. This is Quandamooka sea country and nothing moves without QYAC.

processes.name: Multi-effect distillation, waste heat driven

specific_energy.basis: about 2 kWh electrical per cubic metre for pumping; published multi-effect range 1.5 to 2.5

processes.byproduct_routing: brine to bittern-magnesium-chloride rather than discharge.
processes.notes: 100 cubic metres a day, at about 35 per cent recovery. This does not replace the freshwater lens and is not meant to. It exists so that new industrial demand never comes out of the aquifer. About 50 kWh thermal per cubic metre, taken from the cascade rather than made fresh, plus about 2 kWh electrical for pumping. Read that thermal number carefully: it is raw low grade heat, and because it is recovered rather than generated its work equivalent is far smaller, in the range of 4 to 7 kWh per cubic metre. Quoting the raw figure without that caveat makes multi-effect distillation look worse than it is, and quoting only the work equivalent makes it look better. Reverse osmosis would use about 3.5 kWh electrical per cubic metre instead and no heat, and is the fair comparison.

processes.name: Sand thermal battery charge

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Precedent is real, running and commercial: Polar Night Energy at Kankaanpaa, Finland, switched on in 2022 with about 100 tonnes of builder's sand, a 100 kW heater and 8 MWh of storage, core at about 500 C with edges at 150 to 200 C, delivering heat to a district network. Read that precedent exactly: it runs on air, it delivers heat, and it does not deliver electricity to a grid. This 500 tonne unit is scaled straight off that ratio at about 0.08 kWh per kilogram.

processes.name: Sand thermal battery discharge

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Excellent as heat, poor back to electricity. The 25 to 30 per cent electrical round trip is not demonstrated at this scale and should never be sold as a grid battery. Use heat stores for heat needs and electricity stores for electricity needs; forcing one to do the other's job is where the real losses hide.

processes.name: Waste heat cascade manifold

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Heat only ever flows one way, so this is a staircase, not a circle. Each step uses what the step above had finished with, until the last of it is warming a room. Underground there is no sky to throw it at, which is why the discipline is never to let a hot pipe or a cold pipe dead-end.

processes.name: Enclosed oscillating water column

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Precedent: Mutriku in the Basque Country, 296 kW from 16 turbines built into a working harbour wall, commissioned July 2011, the longest continuously operating plant of its kind. No external moving parts anywhere a living thing can reach, which is this pack's hard rule for anything in the water. The local wave resource assumed here, about 15 kW per metre of frontage, comes from Luke's own energy page and was not independently verified; published national assessments put the northern shelf under 10 kW per metre and the southern half of the country at 25 to 35, with Queensland described as moderate. Footprint is zero because it lives inside a structure that would be built anyway.

processes.name: Bladeless tidal vortex array

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Vortex-induced vibration converters of the VIVACE type work at about 2 knots and have no spinning blades, which fits the no-blade-near-dugongs rule. Research grade, not commercial. Output figures here are a placeholder so the graph has something to hang on, not a performance claim.

processes.name: Bladeless wind harvest

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Catches the breeze with nothing that can strike a bird. Bladeless oscillating masts remain unproven commercially and the numbers here are placeholders. Mounted on existing structures only.

processes.name: Ground freezing station

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Freezing saturated sand takes about 55 kWh thermal per cubic metre: roughly 400 kg of pore water at 334 kJ per kg latent heat plus sensible heat in water and sand. At a brine chiller coefficient of performance around 1.5 down to -30 C that is about 37 kWh electrical per cubic metre. Standard worldwide for shafts and cross-passages in soft wet ground, and the rejected heat is a genuine input to the cascade rather than a loss.

processes.name: Waste plastic pyrolysis
processes.notes: Yields of about 65 per cent oil, 20 per cent gas and 12 per cent char are mid-range for mixed polyolefin feed. Marked disputed on purpose: plastic pyrolysis oil quality, contamination from PVC and additives, and whether the whole route is genuinely better than not making the plastic are all live arguments, and this pack does not pretend otherwise.

processes.name: Chlor-alkali membrane cell
processes.chemistry: 2 NaCl + 2 H2O -> Cl2 + H2 + 2 NaOH

specific_energy.basis: membrane cell, published range 2,300 to 3,000 kWh per tonne of chlorine with a median near 2,600

processes.byproduct_routing: chlorine to chloride-route-chlorination and zircon-chlorination; sodium hydroxide to zircon-caustic-fusion and geopolymer activator; hydrogen to methanol-synth.
processes.notes: Sea salt comes from the desalination brine, which is the only honest local sodium source. This one cell is the hinge of the whole chemistry: everything chlorinated downstream depends on it, and so does the alkali the blocks need.

processes.name: Lime kiln
processes.chemistry: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2

specific_energy.basis: practical lime kiln, thermal; theoretical minimum about 0.89 kWh per kg

processes.notes: Cultural care, non-negotiable: shell for lime may only come from aquaculture waste or a lawful commercial limestone source. Never from a midden, never from any shell deposit that is or may be culturally significant. Where that cannot be assured, this process runs on imported limestone and the pack says so.

processes.name: Brine bittern to magnesium chloride
processes.chemistry: Mg(2+) + Ca(OH)2 -> Mg(OH)2 + Ca(2+); Mg(OH)2 + 2 HCl -> MgCl2 + 2 H2O
processes.notes: The Dow seawater process, run on desalination brine instead of raw seawater so the reject stream becomes the feedstock. Seawater carries about 1.29 g of magnesium per litre; brine at 35 per cent recovery concentrates that to about 2.0 g per kg, and this line recovers about 77 per cent of it. Spent brine still has to go somewhere and its discharge remains a marine ecology question, not a solved one.

processes.name: Magnesium chloride electrolysis
processes.chemistry: MgCl2 -> Mg + Cl2

specific_energy.basis: industry 12 to 18 kWh per kg magnesium, plus dehydration of the feed salt

processes.byproduct_routing: magnesium to kroll-reduction; chlorine back to the chlorinator. This closes the magnesium and chlorine loop.
processes.notes: The catch is the power bill, not the chemistry. Pulling a kilogram of magnesium out of the sea costs 10 to 18 kWh, about what a household fridge uses in a fortnight, and drying the salt first adds more. This pack has not proved the loop needs no top-up chlorine; it needs a full chlorine mass balance across all four chlorinating processes before that claim is made.

processes.name: Ilmenite smelter
processes.chemistry: FeTiO3 + C -> Fe + TiO2(slag) + CO

specific_energy.basis: direct current arc ilmenite smelting, about 800 to 900 kWh per tonne of feed

processes.byproduct_routing: titania slag to chloride-route-chlorination; pig iron to ndfeb-magnet-sinter and general fabrication; carbon monoxide to co-afterburner.
processes.notes: Two useful metals from one grain, which is the waste-nothing idea in a nutshell. Real slag assays around 85 per cent titanium dioxide rather than pure; the balance is iron oxide and gangue and is carried in the slag figure.

processes.name: Fluid bed chlorination to titanium tetrachloride
processes.chemistry: TiO2 + 2 Cl2 + C -> TiCl4 + CO2

specific_energy.basis: fluid bed chlorination, largely thermal

processes.notes: Titanium tetrachloride is a fuming liquid that hits water and turns straight to hydrochloric acid. Not a poison, but a real handling job with sealed lines and scrubbers.

processes.name: Pigment oxidation, chloride route
processes.chemistry: TiCl4 + O2 -> TiO2 + 2 Cl2

specific_energy.basis: oxidation reactor and finishing

processes.byproduct_routing: chlorine returns to chloride-route-chlorination. This is the cleaner of the two pigment routes precisely because the chlorine recycles.
processes.notes: The single biggest thing the world uses these sands for: the white in paint, paper and sunscreen. Also the photocatalytic self-cleaning surface, which is a real property and not a claim about health.

processes.name: Sulfate route pigment (the copperas route)
processes.chemistry: FeTiO3 + 2 H2SO4 -> TiOSO4 + FeSO4 + 2 H2O, then hydrolysis and calcination to TiO2. Shown here as an industry mass ratio, not a balanced equation.

specific_energy.basis: electrical only; the 900 C calciner load is carried as heat

processes.byproduct_routing: copperas to copperas-calcine; weak acid to contact-acid-plant for reconcentration.
processes.notes: Deliberately kept alongside the chloride route as a choice with a real trade-off. This route takes lower grade feed and makes about 3.2 tonnes of iron sulfate, called copperas, per tonne of pigment. At pigment plants worldwide that is a genuine disposal headache. Here it is the feed for the next process, which is the whole argument of the pack in one bucket.

processes.name: Copperas calcination to iron oxide pigment
processes.chemistry: 2 FeSO4.7H2O -> Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3 + 14 H2O

specific_energy.basis: rotary calciner at 700 to 800 C, thermal

processes.byproduct_routing: sulfur dioxide and trioxide to contact-acid-plant, which returns sulfuric acid to sulfate-route-pigment. That is the acid loop closing.
processes.notes: A titanium plant's waste stream becoming the island's red and yellow paint, next to titanium white and biochar black. Colour, not disposal. Said plainly: this is ordinary pigment chemistry and is not a claim about ochre, which means something here that a factory does not get to borrow.

processes.name: Contact process acid plant
processes.chemistry: 2 SO2 + O2 -> 2 SO3; SO3 + H2O -> H2SO4

specific_energy.basis: blowers and pumps only; the reaction is strongly exothermic

processes.notes: Runs part loaded on the copperas calciner's 0.036 kg per minute of sulfur dioxide, so about half its acid still needs elemental sulfur brought in. Naming that shortfall is more useful than pretending the loop closes.

processes.name: Zircon caustic fusion
processes.chemistry: ZrSiO4 + 4 NaOH -> Na2ZrO3 + Na2SiO3 + 2 H2O

specific_energy.basis: fusion at 600 to 650 C

processes.byproduct_routing: sodium silicate liquor to geopolymer-block-press as the alkali activator. The zircon plant's effluent is the builder's reagent.
processes.notes: This is the loop Luke names as the star of the story, and the chemistry does check out: splitting zircon the alkali way leaves soluble sodium silicate, plain water glass, which is exactly the activator a geopolymer needs to set. It is the missing half of the cement-free block recipe.

processes.name: Zircon chlorination
processes.chemistry: ZrSiO4 + 4 C + 4 Cl2 -> ZrCl4 + SiCl4 + 4 CO

specific_energy.basis: chlorination furnace at 900 to 1,200 C

processes.byproduct_routing: silicon tetrachloride to sicl4-aerogel; zirconium tetrachloride to zirconia; carbon monoxide to co-afterburner.
processes.notes: The honest version of the silicon tetrachloride story: it is not a drum of poison nobody wants, industry already sells it into silicones and polysilicon. What the island does is keep it, because the two things it makes are two things the island needs.

processes.name: Zirconia precipitation
processes.chemistry: Na2ZrO3 + 2 HCl -> ZrO2 + 2 NaCl + H2O

specific_energy.basis: precipitation, filtration and drying

processes.byproduct_routing: sodium chloride returns to chlor-alkali. A genuine small circle.

processes.name: Zirconia sintering kiln

specific_energy.basis: sintering at about 1,450 C

processes.notes: Ceramic steel: tunnel boring cutter heads, pump bearings, furnace and kiln linings, blades that never rust, thermal barrier parts. The unglamorous stuff that lets all the other stuff happen, and the reason the refinery can line its own furnaces.

processes.name: Acheson silicon carbide furnace
processes.chemistry: SiO2 + 3 C -> SiC + 2 CO

specific_energy.basis: Acheson process, industry range 6 to 12 kWh per kg

processes.notes: Sand plus carbon in a big electric furnace: the oldest synthetic abrasive there is, made this way since the 1890s. Cutting media, refractory liners, hard facing. Making the grit does not get you a power transistor; that is a different world and it sits in tier 4.

processes.name: Carbothermic silicon furnace
processes.chemistry: SiO2 + 2 C -> Si + 2 CO, at about 2,000 C, with a silica fume loss

specific_energy.basis: submerged arc furnace, industry 11 to 13 kWh per kg of silicon

processes.byproduct_routing: silica fume to the block mix as a pozzolan; carbon monoxide to co-afterburner; silicon to muller-rochow-silicone, aluminium-remelt and siemens-polysilicon.
processes.notes: Sand and carbon in an arc furnace gives silicon about 99 per cent pure. Good enough for alloys and silicones. Nowhere near good enough for a solar cell, and this pack does not pretend the gap is small. About 91 per cent of the silicon reports to metal here and the rest leaves as fume, which is why the inputs are not the clean stoichiometric 2.14 and 0.86 kg per kg. On the energy books: electricity is only about 45 per cent of the total energy into a submerged arc furnace, the rest arriving as chemical energy in the carbon, and only about 30 per cent of the total ends up in the silicon. The rest leaves as off gas and cooling water, which is exactly why this pack recovers it twice: 150 kW as sensible heat into the cascade, and about 248 kW more downstream when the afterburner burns the carbon monoxide.

processes.name: Direct process silicone plant
processes.chemistry: Si + 2 CH3Cl -> (CH3)2SiCl2; then hydrolysis to polydimethylsiloxane + 2 HCl

specific_energy.basis: reactor, distillation and polymerisation

processes.byproduct_routing: hydrochloric acid straight back to methyl-chloride-synth. That routing is the part most versions of this idea leave unsaid.
processes.notes: Sealants, bakeware, medical tubing, gaskets, seals for everything underground. Note the honest chain: this route needs silicon metal, not the chloride, so the extra reduction step is real. The 0.197 kg per minute of acid recovered here nearly covers the 0.202 kg the methyl chloride step needs, so the circle very nearly closes and the small top-up is stated rather than hidden.

processes.name: Methyl chloride synthesis
processes.chemistry: CH3OH + HCl -> CH3Cl + H2O

specific_energy.basis: vapour phase reactor and separation

processes.name: Methanol synthesis from carbon dioxide
processes.chemistry: CO2 + 3 H2 -> CH3OH + H2O

specific_energy.basis: compression and separation only; the reaction is exothermic

processes.notes: The methyl feedstock for silicone, closing carbon into the material stream. Honest gap that Luke names himself: capturing the carbon dioxide in the first place is easy to say and hard to do, and exactly how to catch it is a choice nobody here has made yet. The furnace and afterburner flues are the obvious candidates because they are concentrated, which is the only reason this is marked medium rather than low.

processes.name: Water electrolyser

specific_energy.basis: proton exchange membrane system at the plant boundary, 50 to 58 kWh per kg hydrogen

processes.byproduct_routing: oxygen to pigment-oxidation, contact-acid-plant, co-afterburner and the hyperbaric room. Surplus oxygen from splitting water is normally vented; here it has four jobs.

processes.name: Silicon tetrachloride hydrolysis and supercritical drying
processes.chemistry: SiCl4 + 2 H2O -> SiO2 + 4 HCl, then supercritical carbon dioxide drying

specific_energy.basis: supercritical carbon dioxide drying is the dominant load

processes.byproduct_routing: hydrochloric acid to bittern-magnesium-chloride and methyl-chloride-synth.
processes.notes: Among the best insulation there is, and it is what lets the sand battery hold heat for weeks. The part that decides whether this is a loop at all: hydrolysing silicon tetrachloride throws off four molecules of hydrochloric acid for every one of the chloride, 0.121 kg a minute here. Route it back and the circle closes. Do not, and you have swapped one stream for another.

processes.name: Carbon monoxide afterburner
processes.chemistry: 2 CO + O2 -> 2 CO2
processes.byproduct_routing: carbon dioxide to methanol-synth, algae-photobioreactor and co2-heat-pump.
processes.notes: Every carbothermic furnace in this pack breathes carbon monoxide: 1.045 kg a minute from the silicon furnace, 0.280 from the carbide furnace, 0.091 from zircon chlorination and 0.056 from the ilmenite smelter, which is the 1.472 shown. Burning it at about 10.1 MJ per kg gives roughly 248 kW of high grade heat and turns a toxic gas into the carbon feedstock. This is one of the tidiest joins in the whole graph.

processes.name: Syngas combined heat and power
processes.notes: Pyrolysis gas at about 5.5 MJ per kg gives roughly 40 kW thermal input, which at 30 per cent electrical efficiency is about 12 kW of power and 24 kW of recoverable heat. Combustion mass split is approximate. Negative power means this process is a net generator.

processes.name: Algae photobioreactor
processes.chemistry: CO2 + H2O + light -> biomass (about CH1.8O0.5N0.2) + O2
processes.notes: Translucent columns along a corridor doing the lungs' job: taking in what people breathe out and giving back oxygen while growing biomass. About 1.8 kg of carbon dioxide per kg of dry algae. At a realistic 20 g per square metre per day this needs about 720 square metres to make 14 kg a day, which is why it is a corridor wall and not a jar. Proven at demonstration scale; running it as a corridor's everyday air handling is the integration step nobody has done.

processes.name: Bioplastic extraction from algae

specific_energy.basis: solvent extraction and drying

processes.notes: Polyhydroxyalkanoate for non-structural printing. Yields from algae are strain dependent and 30 per cent is optimistic; treat as modelled. Residue goes back to the digester or the retort.

processes.name: Mycelium panel growing room
processes.notes: Lignocellulose waste grown into rigid composite that chars instead of melting, which matters a great deal in a sealed space. Commercial mycelium packaging and panels already exist. Rate is amortised across a multi-day grow cycle.

processes.name: Aluminium remelt and alloying

specific_energy.basis: induction remelt, about 5 per cent of the 15 kWh per kg of primary smelting

processes.notes: Melting reclaimed aluminium is routine and cheap. Hitting a named structural specification is the harder half, and this pack does not claim it. Drink cans are the wrong alloys to start from, they do not heat treat, and mixed scrap carries tramp iron and copper that never come back out. Silicon from the furnace is the dopant that pulls the melt toward a usable window. Marked low until someone runs a real mass balance on an actual island scrap sample.

processes.name: Steel and copper stream baling
processes.notes: Deliberately not a smelter. No local steel making is proposed anywhere in this pack. Clean and sorted is worth real money and mixed and crushed is worth nothing, so the honest island move is to bale properly and ship a valuable product rather than pay to bury a worthless one.

processes.name: Circuit board recovery line
processes.notes: Boards are the densest ore in the whole stream. Copper, and a small precious metal concentrate rather than pure metal, are the proven catch. Pulling rare earths back out of a magnet is a harder job than pulling gold off a board and far less settled; treat that as a stretch, not a given. Batteries never go in a bin.

processes.name: Transcritical carbon dioxide heat pump

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: The air conditioner is the water heater. Energy closes: 40 kW of work plus 88 kW absorbed from the cooled space is 128 kW rejected, of which 120 leaves as hot water and 8 is lost. R744 transcritical refrigeration runs supermarkets across Europe and Australia today, so the only novelty is feeding it captured carbon dioxide instead of a bottled gas. Underground there is no outside, which turns heat rejection from a cost into the point.

processes.name: Cryogenic air separation unit
processes.byproduct_routing: liquid nitrogen boil-off cold runs the food cold store before the gas goes and does its industrial job.
processes.notes: Air is 23.1 per cent oxygen, 75.5 per cent nitrogen and 1.3 per cent argon by mass, which is the split shown. The deep cold is a by-product of gases the workshop needs anyway, so long term cold storage rides along for the price of some pipe.

processes.name: Kroll reduction to titanium sponge
processes.chemistry: TiCl4 + 2 Mg -> Ti + 2 MgCl2

specific_energy.basis: reduction vessel and vacuum distillation, excluding magnesium electrolysis

processes.byproduct_routing: magnesium chloride to magnesium-electrolysis, which returns both the magnesium and the chlorine. This is the magnesium and chlorine loop.
processes.notes: Three kilograms an hour, about 22 tonnes a year at 7,500 hours. Small on purpose. Counting the whole chain, titanium here costs about 34 kWh per kg: 10 for the reduction, about 18 for the magnesium it eats, and about 6 up the chlorination chain. That is inside the real world range of roughly 30 to 60 kWh per kg for sponge, and it is exactly why a titanium bike frame costs several times a steel one. The metal is not rare here. The electricity is the price.

processes.name: Lateral wall mining head
processes.notes: The boldest idea on the whole ladder, and the frontier line has to be said in one precise sentence: rooms in rock exist, rooms in wet sand do not. SubTropolis in Kansas City is 55 million square feet of business park inside a limestone mine, Coober Pedy has Australians living underground, Helsinki has a formal underground master plan and Singapore stores reserves in rock caverns. All documented, all visitable. Nobody anywhere has made habitable rooms in unconsolidated, water-saturated island sand. This process is the machine that would have to: widening its bore, sorting the excavated sand into minerals and building feedstock, and lining the void it leaves as usable space. Excavation as part refinery, part architecture. It is a drawing.

processes.name: Robotic void lining
processes.notes: Interlocking blocks that clip together like a drystone wall so the lining can shift a little and settle back instead of cracking. The unsolved bit, said plainly, is the seal: whatever the wall is made of it has to hold back wet sand and the water in it for the long haul, and nobody has cracked that.

processes.name: In-situ fused quartz liner
processes.chemistry: Melt, not sinter. Silica must pass 1,713 C to fuse into glass rather than merely bond at the grain edges.

specific_energy.basis: theoretical melt energy about 0.51 kWh per kg (1,690 K of sensible heat plus 160 kJ per kg of fusion enthalpy) at about 35 per cent process efficiency

processes.notes: Melt the sand and it becomes the wall. Note the word: melt, not sinter. A 25 mm glass skin on a 2 m bore is about 345 kg of sand per tunnel metre, so at 15 m a day that is 3.6 kg a minute and about 323 kW of melting power for the lining alone. Holding a continuous melt front behind a moving machine is the part nobody has done, and the wet aquifer face is the other unsolved problem: freeze or dewater first, or print geopolymer instead. This is the single least likely process in the pack and it is kept because it is honestly labelled, not because it is close.

processes.name: Siemens polysilicon reactor
processes.chemistry: Si + 3 HCl -> SiHCl3 + H2, then 4 SiHCl3 -> Si + 3 SiCl4 + 2 H2 at the hot rod

specific_energy.basis: Siemens process, published range 45 to 120 kWh per kg depending on reactor design and plant vintage; 65 taken as a modern plant

processes.byproduct_routing: silicon tetrachloride to sicl4-aerogel and the silicone chain.
processes.notes: The step every glib "solar panels from sand" line skips. The silicon is turned into a gas, distilled and re-deposited pure: the route from 99 per cent to 99.9999 per cent. The chemistry is settled and the scale is the question. Rated here at 1.2 kg an hour, about 9 tonnes a year, against world plants that make 50,000. About 87 per cent of the silicon fed in reports to polysilicon and the rest leaves as the chloride, which is why the aerogel plant has a feedstock at all.

processes.name: Solar cell and module line

specific_energy.basis: cell and module manufacture excluding the polysilicon step

processes.notes: Solar is a stretch but real, unlike the chip fab. A 400 W module weighs about 21 kg of which roughly two thirds is glass, which the island can already make, so the module line is much closer than the cell wafering. Silver paste stays an import. Marked speculative because a cell line is a serious capital facility with clean room process control, not a shed with a press.

processes.name: Monazite caustic cracking
processes.chemistry: REPO4 + 3 NaOH -> RE(OH)3 + Na3PO4, at about 145 C

specific_energy.basis: caustic digestion at about 145 C

processes.notes: Three hundred grams an hour. Deliberately tiny, because this is the grain you treat with respect. Monazite is naturally occurring radioactive material: separating it means licensed handling, monitored workers, contained dust and a plan for the whole decay chain. That is a real cost and a real duty, not a footnote. Australia was once the world's largest producer of monazite, supplying about 70 per cent of the concentrate the western world processed in 1987, with almost all of it exported to France. Australian monazite mining terminated in 1995, after Rhone-Poulenc closed its French processing plant because the cost of disposing of the thorium made extracting the rare earths uneconomic. Australia is still thought to hold the largest monazite resource in the world and has not been a significant producer since. Any restart is a community decision made in daylight, not an engineering one.

processes.name: Rare earth solvent extraction

specific_energy.basis: multi-stage counter-current extraction; energy quoted per kg of separated magnet oxide

processes.notes: The proven route and a harsh one: hot acid, then shaking the metals out between two liquids that will not mix. It is how every rare earth in your phone was separated. It works and it is nobody's idea of clean. Note the split honestly: the magnet metals are only about 17 per cent of what comes out and the plainer cerium and lanthanum are about two thirds. Routing the minority and calling it a loop is a fair criticism of this whole branch.

processes.name: Neodymium iron boron magnet line

specific_energy.basis: calciothermic reduction, strip casting, milling, aligned pressing and sintering

processes.notes: Nd2Fe14B runs about 32 per cent neodymium, 64 per cent iron and around 1 per cent boron by mass, which is the mix shown. These are the magnets in every electric motor and generator on the island, from the gentle harvesters to the workshop tools. Boron is an import.

processes.name: Thorium vitrification and bank

specific_energy.basis: joule-heated melter, glass at about 1,150 C

processes.notes: Locked into glass, banked, stewarded. Not burned. Australian federal law prohibits nuclear power installations under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 section 140A and the Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Act 1998 section 10, and this pack contains no reactor. What the world is doing is worth knowing without pretending it is available here: China's TMSR-LF1 at Wuwei in Gansu, a 2 MW thermal experimental molten salt reactor, reached first criticality in October 2023 and the Chinese Academy of Sciences announced the first thorium to uranium fuel conversion on 1 November 2025. No commercial thorium reactor runs anywhere. The bet here is not that the radioactivity was imaginary; it is that a stewarded reserve is worth the handling where a pile written off never was.

processes.name: Fungal bio-leaching of rare earths
processes.notes: The prize would be doing the acid bath's job with organic acids from fungi at room temperature. Bio-mining is a real research field, but the demonstrations are on soft secondary sources like phosphogypsum and spent catalysts. Monazite is a refractory phosphate whose crystal lattice resists chemical attack, and nobody has bio-leached it at any useful scale. A research question the bench could take on, not a process anyone can cost. The recovery split here is a placeholder.

processes.name: Underground pumped hydro

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: The elegant one: the tunnelling digs voids on its way to making the city and the same voids, sealed and deep, become the lower reservoir with a surface pond above. Kidston in north Queensland already proves a dug-out mine can hold the water, converting two pits of an abandoned gold mine into a 250 MW, 2 GWh store, under construction with energisation expected 2026. The arithmetic here: 50,000 cubic metres through 120 metres of head at 85 per cent turbine efficiency is about 13.9 MWh. The island has the height, with Mount Hardgrave at roughly 219 to 240 metres, but this depends entirely on the aquifer model coming first and on siting nowhere near the natural lakes, which are ruled out first, not last.

processes.name: Silicon carbide power device line

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Turning carbide grit into a power transistor is a different world: you have to grow one flawless crystal straight out of vapour at around 2,500 C and then build a chip factory around it. No rate and no cost are given here because inventing either would be dishonest. Unlocks only through an off-island partner, if ever.

processes.name: Sovereign chip line, 90 to 180 nm

mass_balance_kg_per_min.note: no mass flow: this process moves energy, information or people

processes.notes: Worth being blunt: a wafer fab is billions of dollars and hundreds of process steps, not a bench in a shed. Choosing deliberately old, robust nodes for control and sensing is the right instinct, and it still does not make this near. In the game this exists to be visible and out of reach, which is the honest shape of it.
